### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A25 and A26 each occur exactly once per trace, whereas before they occurred on average 1.58 times per trace, with about 36.5% of traces containing more than one occurrence of each. [OCC001, OCC002]
- The successor distribution of A26 changed: before, about 37% of its outgoing transitions went to A25 and 63% to A20; after, all observed transitions go to A20. [DIR001]
- The relation between A25 and A26 changed: before, A25 preceded A26 in about 64% of traces, and the two were interleaved or repeated in about 37%; after, A25 always precedes A26 and there is no interleaving or repetition. [REL001]
- The gap between A25 and A26 became fixed: before, the gap was one event in about 36% of cases, with some longer gaps; after, the gap is always one event. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process changed so that activities A25 and A26 are no longer repeated or interleaved; they now occur exactly once per case, with A25 immediately preceding A26. All five indicators point consistently to the same underlying difference: the recurrence of A25 and A26 disappeared, A26 no longer routes back to A25, and the order became strictly A25 then A26 with no intervening events. The number of distinct differences (one) clearly exceeds the 0.29 items expected by chance under screening. A competing explanation—that the before window simply captured an unusual sample with a recurring variant—cannot be fully excluded, but the consistency across occurrence, routing, relation, and lag makes that unlikely.
